name: Diapo
title: Diapo · Film camera with a live viewfinder
description: Diapo is a free film camera with no ads: pick a film, see it live in the viewfinder, load rolls that develop later or use the 27-shot disposable camera. No accounts and no internet.
intro: Diapo is a camera for Android. You pick a film before you shoot and see it live in the viewfinder: what you see is what gets saved. For anyone who wants photos that look like film without editing them afterwards.
key_facts: No accounts · No internet permission · Photos never leave the phone · Open source
features: The film shows in the viewfinder before you shoot. What you see is what gets saved, at full resolution.
Summer 98, Cold slide, Expired, Flash night, Classic B&W, Press B&W, Instant, Disposable, Cinema and Toy camera.
Load 12, 24 or 36 shots with a single film. You see none of them until the roll develops, right away or when you choose.
27 shots with a fixed film. Pass the phone around and find the photos together when the roll develops. Inside, the camera changes its look: cardboard, paper and a wheel to wind on.
Share a whole roll as one image, with its perforations and frame numbers. No watermark.
Apply a film to a photo you already have. The original is left untouched.
privacy_summary: Diapo has no accounts, ads or analytics, and it does not ask for the internet permission: it cannot send anything.
The photos of an undeveloped roll are stored encrypted on the phone and only reach your gallery when the roll develops.

faq.question: Is it really free?
faq.answer: Yes. Every film and feature is free, with no ads, no purchases and no watermark.

faq.question: Where can I download it?
faq.answer: It cannot be installed yet: Diapo is being tested on Android, and the iPhone version will come later. This page will say so as soon as it can be downloaded.

faq.question: What happens to an undeveloped roll if I change phones?
faq.answer: Undeveloped photos only exist on that phone. If you uninstall the app, clear its data or move to another phone, they are lost. Develop the roll first.

faq.question: Can I apply a film to photos I already have?
faq.answer: Yes. From the gallery of the app, "Develop photos from your phone" opens the system picker. The original photo is left untouched: a new one is saved.
